analyst_view.overall: Hoffenheim (23rd, 4 pts) host Sturm Graz (24th, 4 pts) in a game both need to stay in the play-off race. Christian Ilzer's side lost 1-0 in Frankfurt on Saturday (10th in the Bundesliga) and Ozan Kabak was sent off there; his Europa League absence through a yellow-card ban is already counted by the numbers. Hoffenheim also miss defenders Valentin Gendrey (broken fibula), Robin Hranáč and Albian Hajdari plus De Cat (per Starting11's availability list; Gendrey's injury is confirmed by LKZ), none of whom the numbers list, with Conté, Wimmer and Prass doubtful. Sturm Graz have no reported injuries but have lost three of their last four (2-3 against Celje, 3-4 against Salzburg, 0-1 at Altach). With no referee named yet, I lean slightly higher on goals and shots on target because Hoffenheim's back line is thinner than the numbers know.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals and already add 6% to Sturm's scoring for Kabak's absence. On top of him Hoffenheim are missing Gendrey, Hranáč and Hajdari at the back, and Sturm have conceded 3 and 4 in recent games, so I go slightly higher, about 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers expect 10.6 corners, 7.1 for Hoffenheim, and already move Sturm's up 4% for recent form. The injuries are mostly in defence and should not change how Hoffenheim attack down the flanks, so I stay at 10.6.

cards.text: The numbers expect 4.0 cards and already add about 10% for Sturm's recent cards. Ilzer called his side immature after Kabak's red in Frankfurt, but Kabak is out and no referee is named yet, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers expect 32.1 shots and already lift both sides for busy recent games (+11% Hoffenheim, +7% Sturm). Nothing new changes the volume, so I stay at 32.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers expect 9.8 shots on target. A patched-up Hoffenheim defence should let Sturm get a few cleaner chances than usual, so I go slightly higher, about 10.1.
